It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Face Coverage Mask Culling](3397-face-coverage-mask-culling.md) by operating at the individual polygon level to identify which geometry is eligible for neighbor interaction, rather than determining how to cull based on coverage masks [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method operates at the individual polygon level to identify eligible geometry for neighbor interaction, rather than using coverage masks to determine culling. The evidence (Source S1) explicitly states that 'Neighbor-based culling only concerns geometry that lies on one of the six voxel-cell boundary planes' and describes classifying a polygon as a boundary polygon by checking its vertices ('individual polygon level'). It further contrasts this with the concept of 'coverage masks' by showing code snippets involving `occlusion` masks but clarifying that the culling logic is restricted to boundary geometry, implying the mask usage is secondary to or distinct from the primary geometric eligibility check described. The evidence supports the distinction between identifying eligible geometry (boundary polygons) versus a generic mask-based culling determination.
supported
